tree.question: What does the EU AI Act require from a mid-size SaaS company building features on third-party LLMs, what applies now vs later, and where is there disagreement?

children.question: Which role does the company hold under the Act?
Is a company that builds features on a third-party general-purpose model a provider of an AI system, a deployer, or both?
When does fine-tuning or modifying a third-party model make the company a provider of a general-purpose AI model?
Which obligations apply from which date?
What has applied since August 2025, including duties on the model providers upstream?
What applies from August 2026, and was any of it postponed?
What must the company concretely do?
What does the AI literacy duty require?
What transparency duties apply to chatbots and generated content?
What extra duties apply if a feature falls in a high-risk use area such as hiring or credit?
What must the model provider give the company, and what can the company rely on?
What are the maximum fines, and how are smaller companies treated?
Where do experts and regulators still disagree?
Should and will the proposed delay and simplification package change the dates?
Is the threshold for becoming a model provider through modification workable?
Are national authorities and technical standards ready for enforcement?
How clear is the line between high-risk and non-high-risk uses?

relation_vocab.name: applies_from
relation_vocab.description: subject = an obligation set (canonical label); object = the instrument that sets the date ('EU AI Act' or 'Digital Omnibus on AI'); value = ISO date YYYY-MM-DD.

relation_vocab.name: proposed_application_date
relation_vocab.description: subject = obligation set; object = the proposing instrument or institution position (e.g. 'Digital Omnibus on AI', 'European Parliament position', 'Council position'); value = ISO date or 'linked to standards availability'.

relation_vocab.name: obliges
relation_vocab.description: subject = role (canonical label); object = obligation (canonical label). No value.

relation_vocab.name: has_role
relation_vocab.description: subject = actor; object = role (canonical label). No value.

relation_vocab.name: becomes
relation_vocab.description: subject = an action (e.g. 'substantial modification of a general-purpose AI model'); object = resulting role. No value.

relation_vocab.name: threshold_share
relation_vocab.description: subject = rule; object = what is measured; value = number in %.

relation_vocab.name: max_fine_amount
relation_vocab.description: subject = infringement type; object = 'maximum fine'; value = number; unit = 'EUR'.

relation_vocab.name: max_fine_turnover_share
relation_vocab.description: subject = infringement type; object = 'maximum fine as share of worldwide annual turnover'; value = number; unit = '%'.

relation_vocab.name: has_status
relation_vocab.description: subject = a document or process; object = 'legislative status' or 'publication status'; value = one of proposed | in negotiation | provisionally agreed | adopted | published | pending.

relation_vocab.name: published_on
relation_vocab.description: subject = document; object = publisher institution; value = ISO date.

relation_vocab.name: position_on
relation_vocab.description: subject = stakeholder (organisation name); object = issue (canonical label); value = one of supports | opposes | mixed | calls for clarification.

relation_vocab.name: enforced_by
relation_vocab.description: subject = obligation set; object = authority type. No value.

relation_vocab.name: states
relation_vocab.description: Fallback for a sourced fact no other relation fits: subject = topic (canonical label); object = a short factual statement (under 25 words). No value.
